Description of the Training Course

The BIM – Introductory Level Training Course is essential for professionals in the Architecture, Engineering, Construction and Operation (AECO) sector. This is important not only because of the benefits the methodology offers in optimising processes, improving collaboration and efficiently managing built assets throughout their life cycle, but also because of the legal requirements expected in the coming years: in Portugal, it is anticipated that, by 2030, the submission of architectural projects for licensing will have to be carried out using the BIM methodology.

Given this scenario, it is essential for professionals in the sector to acquire the skills that will enable them to keep pace with the digital transition and respond to the new demands of the market.

This Training Course has been carefully designed to provide a comprehensive introduction to the BIM methodology, from its fundamental concepts to its practical application. Participants will understand the role of BIM in digitalising the AECO sector, become familiar with applicable regulations and standards, explore collaborative tools and methodologies, and learn effective strategies for its implementation.

Aimed at professionals who wish to deepen their knowledge of the BIM methodology and apply it strategically to their development projects, this course prepares participants to face the challenges of digitalisation and strengthen their competitiveness in the AECO sector.

* Registration deadline: 27 February

Contents

1. Introduction to the BIM methodology and its impact on the AECO sector
Concept, evolution, potential and challenges of the BIM methodology; BIM dimensions and uses.

2. BIM fundamentals and tools, and emerging technologies
Basic concepts: BIM objects, Product Data Templates (PDTs) and classification systems; BIM tools applicable throughout the asset life cycle; Advanced technologies supported by the BIM methodology.

3. Collaboration and interoperability
Interoperability and open standards; the openBIM workflow and its importance in integrating processes.

4. Regulation and standardisation
Main national regulations; the context of international and national standardisation.

5. Information Management and Procurement
Information management according to standards EN ISO 19650-1 and EN ISO 19650-2; Essential contractual elements: Exchange Information Requirements (EIR) and BIM Execution Plan (BEP).

6. Implementing the BIM methodology in organisations
Main challenges and good practices; Implementation process.

Teaching methodology

Synchronous online sessions, lasting 2 hours each (8 hours in total), including a final assessment to consolidate learning.

Theoretical content will be made available to participants.

Important Notes:

* Discount applied to only one person per entity.

This training course is carried out under the DIGITALbuilt – European Digital Innovation Hub project, of which BUILT CoLAB is a member, enabling entities to find solutions that promote their digitalisation at more affordable prices than are usually charged on the market, since they include co-financing from the PRR and the European Union.

To access this training course, the entity to which the participant belongs must meet certain mandatory requirements:

a) Be an SME, Start-Up or Public Administration entity (with a European tax identification number);
b) The invoice will be issued in the name of that entity, following this process: simultaneous issuance of an invoice for €100 + VAT per participant, and a receipt for the DIGITALbuilt support (grant) of 87.5% (VAT is not included in this grant/support and the entity will have to pay it);
c) The entity must also:
• complete and submit a questionnaire on its digital maturity, before and after taking part in this Training Course (for this purpose, the participant will be contacted directly by the BUILT CoLAB team after registration);
• submit a self-declaration ensuring compliance with the €220,000 limit for the company over a three-year period, as set out in paragraph 4 of Article 28 of the RGIC (General Block Exemption Regulation);
• have a regularised situation regarding repayments under European Fund financing, in accordance with paragraph f) of Article 7 of Portaria No. 135-A/2022, of 1 April;
• have a regularised situation with the Tax Authority, in accordance with paragraph e) of Article 177-B of the Tax Procedure and Process Code;
• have a regularised situation with Social Security, in accordance with paragraph e) of Article 213 of the Code of Contributory Regimes of the Social Security Welfare System;
• not be a “company in difficulty” as defined in paragraph 18 of Article 2 of the RGIC.
